title: German Constitutional Court abortion decision
text: BVerfGE 39,1 — Abortion I was a decision of the Federal Constitutional Court of Germany, addressing the issue of abortion in 1975, two years after the United States Supreme Court decision Roe v. Wade.

title: The 2 June Movement kidnaps West German politician Peter Lorenz. He is released on March 4 after most of the kidnappers' demands are met.
text: Peter Lorenz was a German politician of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). In 1975 Lorenz was a candidate for mayor of West Berlin.

title: 27 June–8 July – 25th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 25th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 27 June – 8 July 1975. The Golden Bear was awarded to Adoption directed by Márta Mészáros.

title: Fire on the Lüneburg Heath
text: The fire on the Lüneburg Heath was a major forest fire in 1975 on the southern part of the Lüneburg Heath in west Germany, with various points of origin near Gifhorn, Eschede and Meinersen. To this day, it is the largest known forest fire in the Federal Republic of Germany.

title: German company Coppenrath & Wiese was founded.
text: Coppenrath & Wiese KG is a German food company that is one of the largest manufacturers of frozen bakery products in Europe. The company mainly produces frozen pies, cakes, tortes, tarts and bread rolls.

title: Launch of the Volkswagen Polo, a three-door hatchback which fits into the Volkswagen range below the Golf and is similar in size and concept to the Renault 5 from France.
text: The Volkswagen Polo is a supermini car produced by the German car manufacturer Volkswagen since 1975. It is sold in Europe and other markets worldwide in hatchback, saloon, and estate variants throughout its production run.

title: The Flick affair begins with a share trade where the Flick company sold shares worth 1.9 Billion Deutsche Mark from Daimler AG to the Deutsche Bank.
text: The Flick affair was a West German political scandal of the early 1980s relating to donations by the Flick company, a major German conglomerate, to various political parties, according to Flick manager Eberhard von Brauchitsch, "for the cultivation of the political landscape". title: “Tränen Lügen Nicht” by Michael Holm
text: "Soleado" is a mainly instrumental piece of music composed by Ciro Dammicco under the alias "Zacar", based on his earlier composition "Le rose blu" (1972). The song was recorded in 1974 by Dammico's band, the Daniel Sentacruz Ensemble, and presented at that year's edition of Festivalbar.

title: “You Ain't Seen Nothing Yet” by Bachman-Turner Overdrive
text: "You Ain't Seen Nothing Yet" is a song by Canadian rock band Bachman–Turner Overdrive. The song was written by Randy Bachman for the band's third studio album Not Fragile (1974).

title: “Griechischer Wein” by Udo Jürgens
text: Udo Jürgens was an Austrian composer and singer of popular music whose career spanned over 50 years. He won the Eurovision Song Contest 1966 for Austria, composed close to 1,000 songs, and sold over 104 million records.

title: “Fox on the Run” by Sweet
text: "Fox on the Run" is a song by English glam rock band Sweet, first recorded in 1974. It was the first Sweet single with the A-side written by the band, rather than by producers Nicky Chinn and Mike Chapman, and was their 14th single overall.

title: “Shame, Shame, Shame” by Shirley & Company
text: "Shame, Shame, Shame" is a 1974 hit song written and produced by Sylvia Robinson, performed by American disco band Shirley & Company and released on the Vibration label. The female vocalist is Shirley Goodman, who was one half of Shirley & Lee, who had enjoyed a major hit 18 years earlier, in 1956, with the song "Let The Good Times Roll" for Aladdin Records.

title: “Paloma Blanca” by George Baker Selection
text: "Paloma Blanca", often called "Una Paloma Blanca", is a song written by Dutch musician George Baker (under his real name, Johannes Bouwens) and first recorded and released by his band, George Baker Selection. The single—the title track of the group's fifth album—was released in 1975 with "Dreamboat" (or "Dream Boat") as its B-side.

title: “S.O.S.” by ABBA
text: "SOS" is a song by the Swedish pop music group ABBA, recorded for their eponymous third album ABBA. The track features Agnetha Fältskog on lead vocals, and was written by Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson, and Stig Anderson, and produced by Ulvaeus and Andersson.

title: “Lady Bump” by Penny McLean
text: "Lady Bump" is a pop disco song by Austrian singer Penny McLean, released in 1975. It was a hit for McLean, who was formerly with Silver Convention.

title: “I'm on Fire” by 5000 Volts
text: "I'm on Fire" is a single by the band 5000 Volts. In Germany, the single was released under the group name Airbus.

title: “Dolannes-Melodie” by Jean-Claude Borelly
text: Jean-Claude Borelly is a French trumpeter and composer.
